record.title: Parisi measure of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model with external field
record.locator: Theorem 2.3 and Appendix B; positive-temperature external-field comparison; retain its one-sided coefficient and equality hypotheses

aligned_passages.text: Full support does not force pointwise positive density. For instance, $\gamma(t)=\int_0^t(s-\tfrac12)^2\,ds$ has full Stieltjes support but $\gamma'(\tfrac12)=0$: every interval of positive length has a positive integral, although the integrand vanishes at one point. The quantitative remainder in (5) rules this out for a minimiser. First, the identity $\mathbb E a^2=1$ expresses $\gamma$ as a quotient of continuous moments and then gives smoothness. Only afterwards do we apply the fixed-time spatial estimate to obtain $\gamma'>0$. **Corollary 4 (smooth positive density; [OpenAI (2026a), Corollary 6.4][FS]).** Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1, $\gamma(0)=0$ and $\gamma\in C^\infty([0,1))$, with derivatives at zero taken from the right. Its Stieltjes measure is $\mu_\gamma(dt)=\gamma'(t)\,dt$, and $$ 2\gamma'(t)\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^3] \geq\frac{\gamma(t)^2}{1000}\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^4]>0 \qquad(0[long §9.1](../long/reasoning-record.md#smooth-density-consequence). Now the two differentiated moments are $$ \frac{d}{dt}\mathbb E b^2=\mathbb E[d^2-6\gamma ab^2], \qquad \frac{d}{dt}\mathbb E a^3=\mathbb E[3ab^2-3\gamma a^4]. $$ For a smooth time coefficient, differentiating $q''=\mathbb E b^2-2\gamma\mathbb E a^3$ therefore gives $$ q^{(3)}+2\gamma'\mathbb E a^3 =\mathcal C_\gamma(t). \tag{9} $$ This identity displays the two uses of the same spatial moment. On a plateau, $\gamma'=0$ and $(v,w,z)=c(a,b,d)$ recover (4). For the now smooth minimiser, $q=t$, so $q^{(3)}=0$ and the left side is $2\gamma'\mathbb E a^3$. Proposition 3 supplies the lower bound for this spatial moment. Apply Proposition 3 to the now smooth minimiser. Strict increase and $\gamma(0)=0$ give $\gamma(t)>0$ for $t>0$; (9) therefore gives (7). Strictness follows from $\gamma(t)>0$ and $\mathbb E a^4\geq(\mathbb E a^2)^2=1$. In particular, Cauchy–Schwarz gives $$ \mathbb E a^3\leq\sqrt{\mathbb E a^2\,\mathbb E a^4} =\sqrt{\mathbb E a^4}\leq\mathbb E a^4, $$ so the same inequality implies $\gamma'(t)\geq\gamma(t)^2/2000$ for $0[Long §§9.1–9.2](../long/reasoning-record.md#smooth-density-consequence) retain the smoothness argument and fixed-time transfer, including the common approximation bounds. **Earlier and related estimates.** The backward shape comparisons, transformed density and positive-temperature gap-crossing argument appear in [Lopatto (2026), v3, Propositions 3.6, 7.1 and 9.1][Lopatto]. [H.-B. Chen (2026), Proposition 4.2][Chen] proves the zero-temperature crossing implication $q''=0\Rightarrow q'''>0$ under the minimiser convention of §3.1. [Lopatto's v4, Proposition 5.1 and Corollary 5.6][Lopatto-v4] give qualitative crossing for arbitrary positive-temperature probability measures. In unit-noise coordinates, their cumulative coefficient is $\gamma_\beta=\beta\alpha_\nu$, where $\alpha_\nu(t)=\nu([0,t])$, and the terminal value is $\beta^{-1}\log\cosh(\beta x)$. Every bounded $\gamma\in\mathcal U$ has this form: choose $\beta>0$ with $\beta\geq\sup\gamma$ and put the remaining probability mass at one. Thus the coefficient classes alone do not distinguish the estimates; the terminal datum and the quantitative control through its zero-temperature limit matter. [Lopatto's external-field paper, Theorem 2.3 and §8][Lopatto-field] also uses a fixed-time spatial inequality for support and positive density. At a continuity point, monotonicity supplies its one-sided coefficient bounds; on a smooth full-support interval of the minimiser, its scalar conditions become equalities. Appendix B gives the positive-temperature, zero-field strict-density result. The bound used here instead applies at a nonstationary comparison time and retains an explicit fourth-moment margin through the local replacement with terminal datum $|x|$. The rescaling and exact hypothesis comparisons are in [long §2.3, finite-temperature dictionary](../long/reasoning-record.md#finite-temperature-dictionary).
